Attacks.Name: Mandibles

Abilities.Name: Wall-crawler
Abilities.Description: A giant ant can climb on ceilings and walls as easily as it moves on the ground.

Attacks.Name: Pincer
Attacks.Hit: 1 damage, and the scorpion gains a +2 attack bonus against the same target this turn with its stinger attack.
Attacks.Triggers: Limited use: 2/round, each requiring a quick action. (Hitting the same target twice with pincer gives the stinger attack a +4 bonus.)

Attacks.Name: Close: Swarming bites (1d3 nearby enemies)
Attacks.Hit: 2 damage, and after the attack, the swarm of bats engages one of the targets
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: The target is hampered until the end of its next turn. It can end the effect by attacking the swarm, or if the swarm drops to 0 hp.

Abilities.Name: No opportunities
Abilities.Description: The swarm of bats can’t make opportunity attacks, and enemies can’t make opportunity attacks against it.

Abilities.Name: Swarming resistance
Abilities.Description: Each turn, the swarm of bats gains resist damage 18+ to all damage from attacks by enemies that the swarm did NOT attack that turn.

Attacks.Name: Fangs, wings, and sword
Attacks.Hit: Damage and effect depends on the natural roll
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: The target takes 10 damage from a sword strike, and the bat cavalry pops free from the target and can move as a free action. Natural even miss against a target taking ongoing damage: The target takes 6 damage from clawing wings. Natural odd hit: The target takes 8 damage, and 5 ongoing damage from bat fangs. Natural 2–5: In addition to any other effect, the bat cavalry pops free from the target, and as a free action, it can move to another nearby enemy and make a fangs, wings, and sword attack against it.

Abilities.Name: Resist ranged damage 16+
Abilities.Description: When a ranged attack targets this creature while it’s flying, the attacker must roll a natural 16+ on the attack roll or it only deals half damage. (Shifty spinning bats are hard to hit unless they’re grounded or stuck.)

Abilities.Name: Skittish
Abilities.Description: A bat cavalry engaged with a conscious enemy after attacking it will attempt to disengage and fly into the air if it has a move action remaining that turn.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Blood drinker
Abilities.Description: When the bat cavalry drops an enemy to 0 hp or below, it continues to attack that enemy (until it dies) instead of attacking other enemies.

Abilities.Name: Wall-crawler

Attacks.Name: Bite

Abilities.Name: Wall-crawler

Abilities.Name: Chilling howl
Abilities.Description: Whenever a dire wolf’s attack drops an enemy to 0 hp or below, all dire wolves in the battle can howl as a free action. When the wolves howl, each enemy in the battle takes a penalty to its attacks and all defenses equal to the number of living dire wolves in the battle (max –5) until the end of the attacking wolf’s next turn. New howls extend the duration of the current howl rather than downgrading the howl’s effect if dire wolves have been slain in the meantime.

Abilities.Description: Roll randomly unless you know this beast’s story already.

Abilities.Name: Resist ranged damage 16+

Abilities.Name: Skittish

Abilities.Name: Unwieldy flyer
Abilities.Description: When the goblin bat mage is staggered, it must roll an immediate save. On a failure, it loses its ability to fly until the end of its next turn. If flying near the ground, it lands immediately. If flying far away from the ground, it lands badly and takes 15 damage.

Attacks.Name: Battle-hardened tusks
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 16+: The dire boar can make a bash attack against a different target as a free action.

Attacks.Name: [Special trigger] Bash
Attacks.Hit: The target is weakened (–4 to attacks and defenses) until the end of the boar’s next turn

Abilities.Name: Bestial durability
Abilities.Description: When an enemy’s attack has an effect on the dire boar other than damage, the boar can roll an immediate hard save (16+); on a success, it negates that effect.

Abilities.Name: Last stand
Abilities.Description:
The boar doesn’t die until it reaches –60 hp. While at 0 hp or below but more than –60 hp, it must roll a normal save at

the end of each of its turns; on a failure it dies. (Fighting dire boars always presents a choice for the PCs: pile on damage to drop it to –60 hp, or trust the save roll to go their way.)

Abilities.Name: One random dire feature
Abilities.Description: Use the dire features table.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Furious streak
Abilities.Description: When the dire boar can make a bash attack, if it isn’t engaged with a different enemy, as a free action it can pop free of the enemy engaged with it and move to a nearby enemy to make that bash attack.

Attacks.Name: Fangs
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit against a dazed enemy: The target takes 20 ongoing thunder damage.

Attacks.Name: Close: Thunder screech (1d3 nearby creatures in a group)
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: The target is dazed (save ends).

Abilities.Name: Resist ranged damage 16+

Abilities.Name: Resist thunder 18+

Abilities.Name: Pouncing opportunity
Abilities.Description: When an enemy moves to engage the dire tiger while it’s unengaged, it can meet that enemy halfway and make a pounce atStack as an interrupt action before the target’s attack.

Abilities.Name: Springing attack
Abilities.Description: If the dire tiger is unengaged and moves to engage an enemy (with a springing leap), it can make a pounce attack as a standard action.

Abilities.Description: Use the dire features table.

Attacks.Name: Jagged claws (2 attacks)

Abilities.Name: Close fighting
Abilities.Description: When an enemy fails a disengage check against the dire mantis, the mantis can make an opportunity attack against it.

Abilities.Name: Big but brittle
Abilities.Description: While the dire mantis might rate as a huge monster in terms of size, its stats are based on those for a large monster.

Attacks.Name: Ghostly fangs
Attacks.Hit: 25 negative energy damage, and the target takes +1d8 negative energy damage for each relationship point it has with the bat’s associated icon.

Attacks.Name: Close: Spiraling assault (1d3 nearby enemies)
Attacks.Hit: 22 negative energy damage, and after the attack the wraith bat teleports to and engages with one target it hit.
Attacks.Triggers: Limited use: Regardless of the number of wraith bats in the battle, only one wraith bat can use this attack each round.

Abilities.Name: Ghostly
Abilities.Description: This creature has resist damage 16+ to all damage except force damage, which damages it normally. A wraith bat can move through solid objects but it can’t end its movement inside them.

Attacks.Name: Mandibles
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: If the target is small, the ankheg grabs it. While the ankheg is grabbing a creature, the only legal target for its mandibles attack is the grabbed creature.

Attacks.Name: Close: Acid spit (one nearby enemy, plus any enemy the ankheg has grabbed)
Attacks.Triggers: Limited use: 1/round, as a quick action.

Abilities.Name: Escape speed
Abilities.Description: At the end of the ankheg’s turn, roll a d6. If it’s equal to or less than the escalation die, the ankheg can move again as a free action.

Attacks.Name: Red-hot hammer
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit or miss: 4 ongoing fire damage.

Abilities.Name: Blistering heat
Abilities.Description: When an enemy engaged with the azer attacks it, that enemy takes 2 fire damage.

Abilities.Name: Fighting surge
Abilities.Description: Once per battle when an attack crits the azer but doesn’t kill it, the azer can heal 4d6 hp.

Abilities.Name: Cold haters
Abilities.Description: The azer adds the escalation die to its attacks against a target that is capable of dealing cold damage with a spell, attack, or magic item.

Abilities.Name: Fire resistance 18+
Abilities.Description: When a fire attack targets this creature, the attacker must roll a natural 18+ on the attack roll or it only deals half damage.

Attacks.Name: Burning claws
Attacks.Hit: 2 damage, and 2 fire damage Fiery flier: An unengaged fire bat can move, make a burning contrail attack, and move away from the target as a standard action without taking an opportunity attack from the target.

Abilities.Name: Blistering heat
Abilities.Description: When an enemy engaged with the fire bat attacks it, that enemy takes 2 fire damage.

Abilities.Name: Fire resistance 16+
Abilities.Description: When a fire attack targets this creature, the attacker must roll a natural 16+ on the attack roll or it only deals half damage.

Abilities.Name: Flight
Abilities.Description: Fire bats are agile fliers, especially when riding hot air currents. They slow down a bit away from warmth.

Attacks.Triggers: Limited use: 1/battle, only while the brute is staggered.

Abilities.Description: When a fire attack targets this creature, the attacker must roll a natural 18+ on the attack roll or it only deals half damage.

Attacks.Name: Multi-legged attack (3 attacks, each against a different enemy)
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 16+: The target takes 5 ongoing poison damage.

Attacks.Name: [Special trigger] C: Basilisk’s stare
Attacks.Hit: 5 ongoing poison damage, and the target must start making last gasp saves depending on the basilisk’s type (see below) as it accidentally takes a full look at the basilisk. Constructs and undead are immune to this effect.
Attacks.Triggers: Failed save: The target takes 25 poison damage as its blood turns to poison. Fourth failed save: The target’s body liquefies and they die. Red Basilisk Failed save: The target takes 15 fire damage, and each of the target’s nearby allies takes 5 fire damage as the target’s blood boils under their skin and sprays outward in gouts of liquid fire. Fourth failed save: The target’s body ignites as their flaming skull shoots upward on a jet of burning blood, killing them. Failed save: The target’s blood begins to coagulate and harden, and dust puffs out of their lungs through their mouth. Fourth failed save: The target’s body turns to stone and they die. White Basilisk Failed save: The target begins to evaporate. The target must make an immediate normal save (11+) or it loses a chunk of flesh or a limb, whatever is dramatic but will allow the creature to survive (perhaps with minuses until healed). Fourth failed save: The target’s body explodes into a fine red mist and they die.

Abilities.Name: Basilisk’s stare
Abilities.Description:
When a basilisk hits an enemy that is already taking ongoing poison damage, the basilisk can make a basilisk’s stare attack against the target as a free action.

Abilities.Name: Resist melee damage 18+
Abilities.Description: When a melee attack targets this creature, the attacker must roll a natural 18+ on the attack roll or it only deals half damage. An attacker can ignore this resistance by declaring they are looking directly at the basilisk during the attack. If they do, the basilisk can make a basilisk’s stare attack against them as a free action before the attack. Constructs and undead are not affected by this resistance.

Abilities.Name: Stare-down
Abilities.Description: When an enemy makes a ranged attack against the basilisk, the basilisk can make a basilisk’s stare attack against them as a free action before the attack.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Death breath
Abilities.Description: Each creature engaged with the basilisk at the end of the basilisk’s turn takes 10 poison damage.

Attacks.Name: Gigantic claws (2 attacks)
Attacks.Hit: 15 damage Dual hit: If both claws hit during the same turn, the bulette can make a terrible bite attack during its next turn as a standard action.

Attacks.Name: [Special trigger] Terrible bite
Attacks.Triggers: Miss: 22 damage.

Abilities.Name: Blood frenzy
Abilities.Description: The bulette’s crit range expands to 16+ while the escalation die is 4+.

Abilities.Name: Serious burrower
Abilities.Description: A bulette can burrow incredibly quickly for short distances. They’re renowned for the mounds of dirt and rock they push above them as they surge through the ground like land torpedoes.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Savage response
Abilities.Description: When an attacker scores a critical hit against the bulette and it survives, the bulette can make a terrible bite attack as a free action against one target engaged with it.

Attacks.Name: Charging maw
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even miss: The target pops free from all enemies engaged with it and is vulnerable to all attacks (save ends). Leaping bite: The green bulette gains a +3 bonus to attack and damage with its first attack each battle.

Abilities.Name: Into the earth
Abilities.Description: The first time each round an attack hits the bulette, it can choose to hunker down as a free action. If it does, it gains a +3 bonus to AC and PD until the start of its next turn. Force attacks and opportunity attacks don’t trigger this ability. If the green bulette hunkers down while it’s moving (for example, from a readied action), its movement ends that turn.

Abilities.Name: Blood-frenzy escalator
Abilities.Description:
While at least one creature in the battle is staggered or unconscious, the bulette gains a bonus to its

attacks and damage equal to the escalation die but can’t use into the earth. Creatures that have no blood (constructs, oozes, plant creatures, etc.) don’t trigger this ability.

Abilities.Name: Occasional burrower
Abilities.Description: Like all bulettes, the green bulette can burrow. While above ground, it prefers to move slowly on the surface and rely on its plant- and soil-covered shell to stay hidden until it attacks.

Attacks.Name: Tongue lash and bite (1d3 nearby enemies)
Ranged: Sticky tongue
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: The target pops free from all enemies engaged with it, is pulled into the pit with the dirt-fisher (who engages it), and loses its next move action. Climbing out of the pit requires a move action and a DC 20 check. If the bulette is not in its pit, the bulette pulls the target to itself and engages it.

Abilities.Name: Hole digger
Abilities.Description: A dirt-fisher can burrow incredibly quickly for short distances, but it prefers to attack from within its pre-dug trap-door pit. It usually has a few pits dug nearby if forced to leave its current pit.

Abilities.Name: Into the earth
Abilities.Description: The first time each round an attack hits the dirt-fisher, it can hunker down and pull the lid on its pit shut. If it does, it gains a +3 bonus to all defenses until the start of its next turn, and any creature in the pit takes a –5 penalty to checks to climb out of the pit. Force attacks and opportunity attacks don’t trigger this ability.

Abilities.Name: Nowhere to run
Abilities.Description: The dirt-fisher deals double damage against creatures engaged with it in its pit.

Attacks.Name: Land-shark maw
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: The target takes 10 thunder damage.

Abilities.Name: Blood-frenzy escalator
Abilities.Description: While at least one creature in the battle is staggered or unconscious, the bulette gains a bonus to its attacks and damage equal to the escalation die. Creatures that have no blood (constructs, oozes, plant creatures, etc.) don’t trigger this ability.

Abilities.Name: Earth surge
Abilities.Description: Whenever the bumoorah takes damage from an attack, it rolls a save; on a 16+ it can immediately dive beneath the ground, preventing further attacks against it until it surfaces at the start of its next turn. Force attacks and opportunity attacks don’t trigger this ability.

Abilities.Name: Serious burrower
Abilities.Description: The bumoorah can burrow incredibly quickly for short distances. Bumoorahs are renowned for the dust-spurts and vibrating sound they generate as they shoot through the ground like hungry spears.

Attacks.Name: Pulverizing maw (1d3 enemies)
Attacks.Triggers: Miss: 45 damage.

Abilities.Name: Blood frenzy
Abilities.Description: The deep bulette’s crit range expands by 4 while the escalation die is 4+.

Abilities.Name: Tunnel fighter
Abilities.Description: While fighting in a tunnel with nowhere for its enemies to move but ahead of it, the deep bulette gains the following abilities based on the escalation die:

Abilities.Name: Escalation die is odd
Abilities.Description: When the bulette hits an enemy engaged with it with an attack, that target pops free from it and is hampered (save ends). Escalation die is even: The deep bulette engages each nearby enemy in front of it as it pushes its bulk inexorably forward down the tunnel. Enemies pushed ahead of it this way don’t get to make opportunity attacks.

Attacks.Name: Charging lance
Attacks.Hit: 15 damage, and the target pops free from the centaur
Attacks.Triggers: Hit ’em hard: The crit range of the attack expands by 2 and instead deals 20 damage on a hit if the centaur first moves before attacking an enemy it wasn’t engaged with at the start of its turn. Natural 18+: The target is also dazed until the end of its next turn.

Attacks.Name: Spear
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: The centaur lancer can make a kick attack as a free action.

Attacks.Name: Kick (1d2 enemies engaged with the centaur)
Attacks.Hit: The target takes 5 damage and pops free from the centaur.

Abilities.Name: Harnessed speed
Abilities.Description: The centaur lancer gains a +4 AC bonus against opportunity attacks.

Attacks.Name: Hoof and weapon
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: As a free action, the centaur raider can move and make another hoof and weapon attack against a different nearby enemy (it will take opportunity attacks for moving).

Attacks.Name: Ranged: Short bow
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 16+: The centaur raider can take an additional move action this turn.

Abilities.Name: Harnessed speed
Abilities.Description: The centaur raider gains a +4 AC bonus against opportunity attacks and only takes half damage from opportunity attacks that hit it.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Barreling charge
Abilities.Description:
When the escalation die is even, the centaur raider can use a standard action and a move action to make a sweeping blow attack against multiple enemies as it moves past them (it will take opportunity attacks). It ends this move and attack unengaged.

Sweeping blow +10 vs. AC (1d3 nearby enemies)—15 damage, and the target loses its next move action.

Attacks.Name: Ranged: Longbow
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: The centaur ranger can take an additional move action this turn. Natural 16+: The centaur ranger can make a second (but not a third) longbow attack this turn as a free action.

Abilities.Name: Moving combatant
Abilities.Description:
The centaur ranger gains a +4 AC bonus against opportunity attacks and only takes half damage from

opportunity attacks that hit it. When an enemy makes an opportunity attack against it and misses, that enemy takes 10 damage from a counter-attack.

Abilities.Name: Terrain familiarity
Abilities.Description: Once each round when the escalation die is odd, the centaur ranger can make use of the area’s terrain to its advantage as a free action. It can choose either to gain a +2 attack bonus for its attacks that turn, or to gain a +2 bonus to all defenses against the next attack that targets it by using a flashy or tricky maneuver (leaping off a rock over an enemy, stirring up a hornet’s nest near an attacker, etc.). The target of its attack or a creature attacking it when it attempts this stunt rolls a normal save; on a success, the bonus is negated.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: R
Abilities.Description: Pinning volley +11 vs. AC (2 attacks)—8 damage, and the target is hampered until the end of its next turn

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Natural 18+
Abilities.Description: The target is stuck (save ends) instead of hampered.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Limited use
Abilities.Description: 2/battle.

Attacks.Name: Oozespasm
Attacks.Hit: 3 ongoing damage, or 10 damage if the target is already taking ongoing damage
Attacks.Triggers: Miss: The chaos glorp pops free from all enemies and moves as a free action to engage a nearby enemy taking ongoing damage.

Abilities.Name: Spontaneous chaos
Abilities.Description: When the escalation die reaches 6, the chaos glorp rolls a normal save. If it succeeds, it transforms into a chaos beast with full hit points.

Attacks.Name: Bestial chaos
Attacks.Hit: Damage and effect depends on the natural roll
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: 7 damage, and the chaos beast can make another bestial chaos attack as a free action. Natural odd hit: 15 ongoing damage. Miss: The chaos beast pops free from all enemies and moves to engage a random nearby enemy as a free action, preferably one it wasn’t just engaged with.

Abilities.Name: Chaos combined
Abilities.Description: Once a chaos beast is staggered, it can combine with another chaos beast next to it as a quick action to become a full-strength chaos brute acting on this beast’s initiative. Replace the other beast with a chaos glorp mook.

Attacks.Name: Brute chaos
Attacks.Hit: Damage and effect depends on the natural roll
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: 25 damage. Natural odd hit: 15 ongoing damage. Miss: 1d3 random nearby enemies each take 10 psychic damage.

Abilities.Name: Chaos combined
Abilities.Description: Once a chaos brute is staggered, it can combine with another chaos brute or chaos beast* next to it as a quick action to become a full-strength chaos behemoth: the new creature rolls initiative as if it had just entered the battle. If a chaos beast and a chaos brute combine to create a chaos behemoth, the behemoth starts with 70 hp instead of 90 hp and takes a –1 penalty to all attacks and defenses.

Attacks.Name: Behemoth chaos
Attacks.Hit: Damage and effect depends on the natural roll
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: 30 damage, and the chaos behemoth can make a mewhowlwail attack as a free action. Natural odd hit: 25 ongoing damage. Miss: 10 damage, and the target is hampered until the end of its next turn.

Attacks.Name: Mewhowlwail (each nearby enemy)
Attacks.Hit: 10 psychic damage, and if the target is taking ongoing damage, saves against that ongoing damage become hard saves (16+)

Abilities.Name: The betrayal of flesh
Abilities.Description: When a nearby enemy taking ongoing damage drops to 0 hp or below, add +15 to the amount of ongoing damage that enemy is taking as its body melts and warps. At the GM’s option, a creature slain in a battle involving a chaos behemoth might transform into a chaos glorp or chaos beast instead of having the decency to just die.

Attacks.Name: Fangs, claws, and horns (3 attacks)
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 14–15: The target is dazed until the end of the chimera’s next turn from a headbutt. Natural 16–17: The target takes 20 ongoing damage from raking claws. Natural 18–20: The chimera can make a fiery breath attack as a free action.

Attacks.Name: [Special trigger] Fiery breath (up to 3 nearby enemies in a group)
Tusk charge
Attacks.Triggers: Limited use: Once the chimera has damaged an enemy with this attack, it can’t use tusk charge again until it drops an enemy to 0 hp or lower. (F) Too many horns: The horns and tusks of the chimera lock together at inopportune moments. When it rolls a natural 1–5 with an attack against multiple targets, it loses any further attacks that turn. (B) Eagle wings: The chimera can fly like an eagle, swooping in and out of the battle. (F) Vulnerability, negative energy: The crit range of negative energy attacks against the chimera expands by 2. (B) Poison fangs: When the chimera rolls a natural 1–5 with an attack and misses, the target takes 20 ongoing poison damage. (F) Bickering heads: The first time each turn the chimera hits with an attack, it rerolls the attack and takes the lower roll.

Abilities.Name: Chimerical change
Abilities.Description:
At the start of battle each PC rolls one icon relationship die of their choice and one die chosen from their

relationships by the GM. A roll of 6 means the chimera has shifted in a manner that gives it a chimerical flaw (F) that the adventurers can exploit. A roll of a 5 indicates that the chimera gains both a flaw and a benefit associated with that icon. A result of 1 or 2 means that the chimera gains the icon’s chimerical benefit (B) without the flaw. Actual benefits and flaws are up to the GM, and should reflect the icons with which the players have relationships.

Abilities.Name: (B) Bearded spell-eating head
Abilities.Description:
When a spell attack misses the chimera, it has no miss effect and the chimera heals 40 hp. (F) Vulnerability, melee: The crit range of melee attacks against the chimera expands by 2. (B) Skin of indomitable faces: When the chimera saves against a condition, it becomes immune to that condition until the end of the battle. (F) Vulnerability, spells: The crit range of spell attacks against the chimera expands by 2. (B) Flaming oil glands: When a creature is engaged with the chimera at the start of its turn, it takes 20 fire damage. (F) Overconfident predator: Each time the chimera scores a critical hit, it takes a cumulative –2 penalty to all defenses. Abilities.Name: Structural collapse
Abilities.Description: While the skin devil is staggered, when an enemy damages it, it loses an additional 4 hp as the hapless thing fails to hold its boneless, bulky mass together.

Abilities.Name: Weakling
Abilities.Description: When building battles using this monster, it only counts as half a normal monster.

Abilities.Name: Free-form covert ability—Unnoticed
Abilities.Description: The skin devil is routinely able to pass through civilized areas without alerting dogs, bouncers, city guards, or passersby. If the thing attacks, that’s when you notice that it’s not a human but a monstrous pile of flesh. In addition to passing unnoticed in crowds, it uses its fluid shape to sneak through hidden places, and it doesn’t make much noise unless it wants to. PCs looking for the devil won’t find it unless they have some special information or advantage, and even then it’s a hard check (DC 25). Normally when PCs think they have the devil cornered, it escapes through a tight exit that it had previously identified.

Abilities.Description: When a lemure is targeted by an attack against MD, it ignores any effects of the attack and only takes damage from it. In addition, lemures fight in a straightforward way, without tactics. They never disengage willingly, and they’re not coordinated enough to concentrate attacks on a vulnerable target.

Abilities.Name: Free-form ability—Mass
Abilities.Description: Heedless of each other’s safety or their own, lemures use sheer numbers to press through locked doors, climb walls, or dog pile on defenders.

Abilities.Description: At the start of the lemure mob’s turn, roll a d6 for each lemure in the mob that’s dropped this battle. For each 6, one of them reassembles its horrid self and stumbles back into the melee that turn (add 13 hit points to the mob’s hp total). To make sure a downed lemure is truly dead, an attacker can spend an additional 7 damage of the total dealt to finish the job instead of carrying that damage over to another lemure in the mob. Expending the right sort of limited-use power, such as a daily spell, might also keep a number of downed lemures totally dead. Once the last member of the mob drops, stop rolling to see if lemures rise up.

Abilities.Description: If the hydra has at least two gnashing teeth attacks left during a turn, it can expend one of those attacks to move to engage a nearby enemy as a free action (but it will take opportunity attacks for doing so).

Abilities.Name: Sprout sixth head
Abilities.Description: The first time the hydra is staggered, as a free action it gains 40 hit points and a sixth gnashing teeth attack, and is considered undamaged at its new hit point total. Using the hydra’s current hit points as a new baseline, the hydra will be staggered again when it drops below 50% of that total.

Abilities.Description: The second time the hydra is staggered, as a free action it gains 40 hit points and a seventh gnashing teeth attack, etc. Use a new hit point baseline as before, but there is no eighth head waiting to sprout.

Dropping an ogre mage to 0 hp doesn’t kill it if it has any uses of regeneration left.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Ki
Abilities.Description: Gain 1d4 ki at the start of each battle. Spend a point of ki as a free action, once per round, to change the ogre mage knight’s natural attack result by one; a natural 1 could become a 2, a natural 19 could become a natural 20, and so on.

Attacks.Name: Naginata
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 18+: Make a second naginata attack against a nearby enemy as a free action (engaging it is not required) Limited use: 1/day, and the attack affects the ogre’s allies engaged with or between enemy targets.

Abilities.Name: C
Abilities.Description: Cone of cold + 13 vs. PD (up to 3 nearby enemies in a group)—50 cold damage

Abilities.Name: Aura of treachery
Abilities.Description: Once per round when a nearby enemy misses the ogre mage with an attack, the ogre mage can make an aura of treachery attack against it as a free action.

Abilities.Name: [Special trigger] C
Abilities.Description: Aura of treachery + 13 vs. MD—the target is confused until the end of the ogre mage’s next turn

Abilities.Name: Flight
Abilities.Description: The ogre mage flies using the sheer power of its superior mind.

Abilities.Name: Invisibility
Abilities.Description: If the ogre mage is not engaged, it can turn invisible as an at-will standard action. It becomes visible when it attacks. The ogre mage takes 1d10 damage each time it uses invisibility while it’s staggered.

Abilities.Name: Resist exceptional attacks 16+

Attacks.Name: Naginata (2 attacks)
Attacks.Triggers: Miss: 15 damage.

Attacks.Name: Ranged: Lightning from torn sky (up to 2 nearby enemies, plus one far away enemy, if any)
Attacks.Triggers: Limited use: 1/battle, but the ogre lightning mage regains the use of this attack if it’s expended each time it uses its naginata attack.

Attacks.Hit: 25 psychic damage First natural even hit each attack: The ogre lightning mage can cancel one spell or magical effect created by the target.

Attacks.Triggers: Natural 2–5: The prismatic ogre mage can use prismatic blast as a free action without provoking an opportunity attack.

Attacks.Hit: 10 force damage, and the target pops free from the ogre mage
Attacks.Triggers: Quick use: This power only requires a quick action (once per round) instead of a standard action when the escalation die is odd.

Attacks.Name: Ranged: Prismatic blast (1d3 nearby or far away enemies in a group)
Attacks.Hit: Roll a d8 against each hit target to determine the type of ray and effect 1. Red: 75 fire damage; Miss: 40 fire damage. 2. Orange: 50 damage, and the target is confused (save ends). 3. Yellow: 40 ongoing poison damage. 4. Green: The target loses a recovery, and the prismatic ogre mage heals 70 hp. 5. Blue: 60 lightning damage, and make a secondary attack: +15 vs. PD (one enemy near the target)—20 lightning damage. 6. Cyan: The target is stunned (save ends). 7. Purple: The target is dazed and confused (save ends both). When the target saves, it takes 40 psychic damage. 8. Magenta: The target is transported into the future. Remove that creature from play, returning it to the battle in (or near) its previous location at the end of its next turn. No time seems to pass for the target while it’s gone.

Abilities.Name: Resist exceptional attacks 16+
Abilities.Description: When a limited attack (not an at-will attack) targets this creature, the attacker must roll a natural 16+ on the attack roll or it only deals half damage.

Abilities.Name: Warp
Abilities.Description:
The prismatic ogre mage warps reality with its presence. Each character hit by the prismatic blast attack during battle must write down one true personal trait or preference about their character such as: “Yellow hair,” “Afraid of spiders,” “Prefers white wine to red,” or “Tattoo of a halfling on left

bicep.” These personal traits are shuffled and randomly distributed equally by the GM after the battle is over. Whichever trait each player receives is now true for their character as well as for the character of the player who wrote it down (unless there has somehow turned out to be a swap…). These traits don’t alter game mechanics (feats, powers, backgrounds, icon relationships, attributes, bonuses, etc.). They are personal details that have been warped and scrambled by the prismatic ogre mage’s magic.

Attacks.Name: Close: Acid-drenched pseudopod (up to 4 attacks, each against a different nearby enemy)
Attacks.Hit: 30 acid damage, and 10 ongoing acid damage
Attacks.Triggers: Miss: 10 acid damage.

Abilities.Name: Climber
Abilities.Description: A black pudding sticks to ceilings and walls when it wishes, sliding along as easily as on the floor.

Abilities.Name: Slippery
Abilities.Description: The pudding has resist weapons 12+.

Attacks.Name: Shlup’n’schlorp
Attacks.Hit: 30 acid damage, and the cube engulfs the target (functions like a grab) if it’s smaller than the cube
Attacks.Triggers: Miss: The cube can make a spasms attack as a free action.

Attacks.Name: [Special trigger] C: Spasms (up to 2 attacks, each against a different nearby enemy)

Abilities.Name: Engulf and dissolve
Abilities.Description: Targets engulfed/grabbed by the cube take 30 acid damage at the start of the cube’s turn but are not viable targets for additional attacks by the cube. Multiple targets can be held within the cube simultaneously. Any engulfed creature that is also staggered must begin making last gasp saves or become paralyzed as the cube’s toxins overwhelm it.

Attacks.Name: Close: Acid-drenched pseudopod (1d4 attacks, each against a different nearby enemy)
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit or miss: 3 ongoing acid damage.

Abilities.Name: Splitter
Abilities.Description: The first time an ochre jelly takes 20 or more damage from a single attack, it splits into two normal-size ochre jellies, each with half the original’s current hit points plus 2d6 hp. Treat the new jellies as undamaged jellies at their new hit point totals without the splitter ability.

Attacks.Name: Jagged sword
Attacks.Hit: 6 damage Dangerous: The crit range of attacks by orcs expands by 3 unless they are staggered.

Attacks.Name: Greataxe
Attacks.Hit: 8 damage Dangerous: The crit range of attacks by orcs expands by 3 unless they are staggered.

Abilities.Description: When an orc berserker drops to 0 hp, it does not immediately die. Ignore any damage in excess of 0 hp, roll 2d6, and give the berserker that many temporary hit points. No other healing can affect the berserker or give it more temporary hit points. When the temporary hp are gone, the berserker dies.

Attacks.Name: Spear
Attacks.Hit: 6 damage Dangerous: The crit range of attacks by orcs expands by 3 unless they are staggered.

Attacks.Name: Ranged: Battle curse (1d3 nearby enemies)
Attacks.Hit: 4 psychic damage, and for the rest of the battle, melee attacks by orcs deal +1d4 damage against the target (non-cumulative)

Attacks.Triggers: Natural 1–5: Reroll the attack against a random nearby creature. If the rerolled attack is also a natural 1–5, the orcish archer takes 3 damage from sheer agonized frustration, but it doesn’t get to make another attack.

Abilities.Name: Final frenzy
Abilities.Description: When the escalation die is 3+, the orcish archer gains a +3 bonus to melee attacks and melee damage

Attacks.Name: Obsidian knife
Attacks.Hit: 4 damage, and +1d4 damage for each other orc engaged with the target (max +4d4)

Abilities.Name: Hears everything
Abilities.Description: Increase the DC to sneak past cave orcs silently by +5.

Abilities.Name: Nocturnal predator
Abilities.Description: If the battle is at night (or in darkness), the orc gains a +2 attack bonus. If the battle is during the day (or in daylight) it takes a –2 penalty to all defenses.

Attacks.Name: Huge spiked flail
Attacks.Triggers: Natural roll is above target’s Constitution: The target catches a disease (see below).

Abilities.Name: Note
Abilities.Description:
When a creature contracts a death-plague orc disease, roll a d4 for the disease type and a d6 for that disease’s symptoms after the battle. Until cured, at the start of each day (after each full heal-up) the PC makes a Constitution check (including any appropriate background) to determine the severity of the disease for that day, or if the PC is cured.

Full bed rest under the care of a healer reduces severity roll from a d6 to a d4 (so a severity check result of 18 would be 1d4 + 2 not 1d6 + 2). A PC under the care of and experience healer or someone who knows healing magic gains a +10 bonus to the Constitution check. At the GM’s option, special ingredients or healing items, found via quest, can give additional bonuses to the check.

Abilities.Name: Disease Type (d4) 1
Abilities.Description: Filthy Fever (d6 roll for symptoms that day) 2:      Chatter Pox (d6 roll for symptoms that day) 3:      Slug Scourge (d6 roll for symptoms that day) 4:      Red Fever (d6 roll for symptoms that day)

Abilities.Name: Filthy Fever Symptoms (d6) 1
Abilities.Description: Slight temperature. 2–3: The runs. You gain 1 less recovery than normal after a full heal-up due to fluid loss. 4+:     You have a hacking cough that sounds like insane laughter and are losing fluids. You gain 2 fewer recoveries than normal after a full heal-up and can’t remain silent.

Abilities.Name: Chatter Pox Symptoms (d6) 1
Abilities.Description: Unsightly and painful sores, occasional shivers. 2–3: Running sores, shivering and chattering teeth. You take a – 3 penalty to social skill checks and to attack rolls with spells. 4+:     Infected sores, fever dreams. Your constitution is weakened. After each full heal-up, roll 1d4 + 3 to determine your starting maximum recoveries for that day. Each time you cast a spell that isn’t at-will, there’s a 25% chance it fails (but you don’t expend the spell).

Abilities.Name: Slug Scourge Symptoms (d6) 1
Abilities.Description: Extreme appetite, nausea. 2–3: Vomiting up slugs. Whenever you make a non-combat Charisma check, roll 2d20 and take the lower result. 4+:    The slugs are inside your lungs! After each quick rest, you lose 25% of your maximum hit points. If you drop to 0 hp this way, you enter into a coma until the next day.

Abilities.Name: Red Fever Symptoms (d6) 1
Abilities.Description:
Scarlet stripes on the eyeballs, itching, buzzing in ears. 2–3:    Blurred vision. You take a –3 penalty to ranged attacks. 4+:     Fever, rage, and confusion. Whenever you roll a natural odd attack roll, you are confused until the end of your next turn. Ranged attacks have a 25% chance of accidentally targeting an ally (check before making the attack roll).

Abilities.Description: When an orc rager drops to 0 hp, it can make a final attack as a free action. (These extra attacks can come from ragers engaged with a PC.)

Attacks.Triggers: Natural 11+: The cadre can make a second double axe attack (no more) as a free action. Dangerous mooks: The crit range of melee attacks by great fang cadre orcs expands by 3 until half the great fang cadre mob has been dropped.

Attacks.Name: Ranged: Big, black, creaking bow
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit or miss: The attack targets PD instead of AC.

Abilities.Description: Whenever an attack eliminates one or more members of the mob, there is a 50% chance that each survivor gains one of these abilities: extra melee attack, damage aura: 1d20 damage vs. any enemy that starts its turn engaged with the orc, or +4 bonus to AC.

Attacks.Name: Grasping tentacles (2 attacks)
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: The otyugh can grab the target. Natural 18 or 20: The otyugh can grab the target and make a big toothy maw attack against it as a free action.

Attacks.Name: Big toothy maw (one enemy it’s grabbing; includes +4 grab bonus)

Abilities.Name: Trash nest defense
Abilities.Description: The otyugh gains a +2 bonus to all defenses while fighting in its nest or in similar piles of excrement and trash.

Abilities.Name: Tentacle flail
Abilities.Description: Once per round, an otyugh can make a grasping tentacles attack as a free action against a moving nearby creature it is not engaged with; on a natural even hit, the target is grabbed and its movement stops.

Attacks.Name: Rip and peck
Attacks.Hit: 15 damage, and until the end of the owlbear’s next turn, the target is hampered (makes only basic attacks) while engaged with the owlbear Vicious hybrid: If the escalation die is even, make another rip and peck attack.

Abilities.Name: Feed the cubs
Abilities.Description: An owlbear that scores a critical hit against a hampered enemy tears a piece of the creature off (GM chooses a limb) and will subsequently attempt to retreat with the prize to feed its cubs. The torn-up enemy is stunned until the end of its next turn.

Abilities.Name: Silent hunter
Abilities.Description: Owlbears are nearly silent until they strike. Checks to hear them approaching take a –5 penalty.

Attacks.Name: Phasing fangs (2 attacks)
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: The spider can make a rummage and filch attack against the target as a free action, even if the target isn’t staggered.

Attacks.Name: Rummage and filch (one staggered creature)
Attacks.Hit: the phase spider steals a random true magic item from the target (see below).

Abilities.Name: Phasing abilities
Abilities.Description: As long as it didn’t just return from being out of phase, at the start of the phase spider’s turn, roll a d6 to see which of its phase and teleport abilities it can access that turn. The spider doesn’t have to use the available ability and can attack normally, if it wishes. 1–2: Short teleport—As a move action, the spider can teleport anywhere it can see nearby. 3: Long teleport—As a move action, the spider can teleport anywhere it can see nearby or far away. 4–5: Phase out—As a move action, the spider can remove itself from the battlefield, returning on its next initiative turn anywhere it chooses nearby. It doesn’t get to make a phase roll at the start of its next turn though. 6: Teleport away—If the spider has stolen at least one magic item, as a move action it can teleport back to its lair, or to its master if it has one. It leaves the battle. If it hasn’t stolen an item yet, it won’t leave and can use its choice of the other abilities this turn.

Abilities.Name: Stolen items
Abilities.Description: If the spider is slain before it leaves battle, all items stolen from the party are recovered. If a d20 roll results in a 20, other magic items are found.

Attacks.Name: Diminutive sparkly sword
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 16+: The pixie warrior can make a madness attack against the target as a free action.

Attacks.Name: Ranged: Enchanted bowshot
Attacks.Hit: 4 psychic damage, and the pixie warrior can make a madness attack against the target as a free action.

Attacks.Name: [Special trigger] Madness
Attacks.Hit: The target is maddened until the end of the pixie’s next turn. The first thing the creature does on its turn is use a standard action to make a display of power that has no practical benefit. The GM chooses the attack, spell, or other power, which should be the most powerful one the character has, preferably a daily. The target expends the power in a great show of prowess, aimed for display rather than effect. Wizards cast their fireballs into the sky, monks demonstrate flawless form while shadow-boxing, and clerics bless the very stones underfoot instead of allies. When the madness effect gets old, substitute any of the following effects, by choice or at random: 1: You love pixies and hate those who threaten them. The target is confused until the end of the pixie’s next turn. 2: Brains knocked loose. The target takes 4 psychic damage each time it takes an action (save ends; yes that could be 3 times per round or more). 3: Reality bender. The target takes 5 ongoing psychic damage. Each time the target fails the save, the ongoing damage increases by 5, cumulative. 4: Massive attack on the unconscious mind. The target chooses one: either let the onslaught slam its mind (take 15 psychic damage), or steel its mind against the onslaught (stunned until the end of the pixie’s next turn). 5: Compulsion to dance. The target takes 5 ongoing psychic damage (no save) until it spends a standard action to dance maniacally. Dancing ends all such ongoing damage, even if the target has been hit multiple times with this effect. 6: Pacifism. The target can’t attack until the end of the pixie’s next turn.

Abilities.Name: Dazzling lights
Abilities.Description: During battle, pixies fill the air with the light and sound of countless flashy illusions. The effects are disorienting enough that the PCs don’t get to add the escalation die to their attacks.

Abilities.Name: Flight
Abilities.Description: Pixies make flying look like a lot of fun.

Abilities.Name: Invisibility
Abilities.Description: When an enemy attacks a pixie and misses, the pixie turns invisible until the start of its next turn (even if it makes opportunity attacks). A pixie can also turn invisible as a standard action, in which case the invisibility still lasts until the start of its next turn.

Attacks.Name: Attack name
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 1–5: The claw flower takes 1d4 damage from burst roots.

Attacks.Name: Close: Bumble spores (1d2 nearby random non-plant creatures)
Attacks.Hit: The effect depends on the roll
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: 4 psychic damage, and the target is confused until end of its next turn. Natural odd hit: 3 psychic damage, and the target is stuck until end of its next turn. Miss: 2 psychic damage.

Abilities.Name: Immobile until pressed
Abilities.Description: The claw flower has roots and normally can’t move, but when it takes 10 or more damage from a single attack it can move normally during its next turn.

Abilities.Name: Spore escalator
Abilities.Description: The claw flower adds the escalation die to its bumble spores attack rolls.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Gentle roar
Abilities.Description: Once per battle, the claw flower can make a bumble spores attack as a quick action.

Attacks.Name: Needle sword
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: The target can’t choose to search for the pixie-pod plant until all podlings in the battle are slain.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Flight
Abilities.Description: The podling that can fly, hovering out of reach and firing arrows.

Attacks.Name: Devouring maw
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: The target is swallowed whole if it’s smaller than the worm (see below). Miss: Half damage.

Attacks.Name: Close: Mighty thrash (1d3 random nearby enemies)
Attacks.Triggers: Miss: Half damage. Natural 1–5: The worm takes 10 damage (but it still deals miss damage on a 2–5). Limited use: The worm can make this attack as a free action if it has no enemies swallowed after using its standard action during its turn.

Abilities.Name: Swallow whole
Abilities.Description: While a creature is swallowed whole, it takes 7d10 acid damage at the start of its turn and is stuck, hampered, and unable to attack or affect anything outside the worm’s stomach (and vice-versa). Most teleport abilities don’t work because you’re hampered and you can’t see the location out of the worm you want to teleport to. There are two ways out. Cut your way out: Deal 40 damage to the worm with a single attack and you can cut your way out. All edged or bladed weapons are reduced to d6 damage dice (at most) inside the worm’s gullet, so good luck. At least you’ll be damaging the worm attacking it from within. Get upchucked: While the worm is staggered, you can use a standard action to try and crawl out of its mouth. Roll a hard save (16+); on a success, the worm vomits you out and spits you somewhere nearby. The worm also vomits out all creatures it has swallowed when it drops to 0 hp.

Abilities.Name: Burrow
Abilities.Description: As the standard monster ability.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Larval feeding
Abilities.Description: The worm’s stomach also includes a mob of larval mooks (purple larvae or parasitic lightning beetles). Feel free to add this nastier special if a PC acts dismissive about the possibility of being swallowed by the worm. Resist most energy damage 16+: Purple worms generate weird energy resistances thanks to underworld radiation and their odd diets. Roll a d8 twice, in secret, to determine what energy types the worm is not resistant to. The PCs probably have to find out what energy works best against the worm the hard way, though you might have mercy and allow a DC 35 Wisdom skill check to figure out what energy types work against the worm. 1: acid; 2: cold; 3: fire; 4: lightning; 5: thunder; 6: holy; 7: negative energy; 8: poison.

Attacks.Name: Mouthparts
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit or miss: The target also takes 5 lightning damage.

Attacks.Name: Ranged: Lightning zap (one nearby enemy not engaged with a purple worm, purple larvae, or parasitic beetle)
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit or miss: The target takes 5 extra lightning damage.

Abilities.Name: Flight
Abilities.Description: The beetles fly badly, usually just enough to get back to the worm when they’ve been shaken off from their hiding spots in its segments.

Abilities.Name: Scaredy bugs
Abilities.Description: Whenever one or more parasitic lightning beetles drop to 0 hp, roll a d6. If you roll less than or equal to the number of beetles that were destroyed by that attack, all beetles in the battle stop fighting, using all their actions during their next turn to disengage and fly away.

Attacks.Name: Bitey maw
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit or miss: The larvae can make a tail stinger attack against a random enemy engaged with it as a free action.

Abilities.Name: Merge with worm
Abilities.Description: Purple larvae can dig quickly in and out of the skin of the purple worm as if they were burrowing but without needing die rolls to succeed.

Attacks.Name: Devouring maw
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: The target is swallowed whole if it’s smaller than the worm (see below). Miss: Half damage.

Attacks.Name: Tail sting (up to 2 random nearby enemies)
Attacks.Triggers: Miss: 20 damage.

Attacks.Name: Prodigious thrash (1d4 random nearby enemies)
Attacks.Triggers: Miss: Half damage. Natural 1–2: The worm and any creatures it has swallowed take 8d6 damage (but it still deals miss damage on a 2). Limited use: The worm can make this attack as a free action if it has one enemy swallowed or less after using its standard action during its turn.

Abilities.Description: As the standard monster ability, but with a +5 bonus to the check.

Attacks.Name: Stabby knife
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 16+: The target also takes 2 ongoing damage.

Attacks.Name: Ranged: Smashy slingstone
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 18+: The target can’t cast a spell until the end of its next turn or until the splotchcap drops to 0 hp, whichever comes first.

Attacks.Name: [Special trigger] C: Pop-out and stab ‘em (one nearby enemy)
Attacks.Triggers: Miss: Damage equal to the escalation die.

Abilities.Name: Impossible teleport
Abilities.Description: When the splotchcap scores a critical hit OR when a PC or a player at the table says the bad word, the splotchcap can teleport to a nearby hidden location it can see as a free action.

Abilities.Name: Pop-out surprise
Abilities.Description: When the splotchcap starts its turn and no enemy can see it, it can make a pop-out and stab ‘em attack that turn as a standard action.

Attacks.Name: Twin skinning knives (2 attacks)
Attacks.Triggers: Miss: Damage equal to the escalation die.

Attacks.Name: Stompy iron boots (one staggered or unconscious enemy)
Attacks.Triggers: Miss: 5 damage.

Attacks.Name: [Special trigger] C: Pop-out and ride ‘em (one nearby enemy)

Abilities.Name: Nastier: F*** T***

Attacks.Name: Big bloody axe (2 attacks)

Abilities.Name: Oh no oh no
Abilities.Description: When a PC or a player at the table says the bad word, the crustycap can take an extra standard action during its next turn. Feel free to let the extra actions stack a few times if someone gets cocky.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Just plain mean
Abilities.Description: When the crustycap scores a critical hit OR when a PC or a player at the table says the bad word, the crustycap can teleport away as a free action. Far away, even to a location it can’t see, and out of the battle. Then at the start of the PCs’ next battle, it teleports back and attacks the PCs, no matter what enemies they are fighting. It will continue to use this power if it can until the PCs take a full heal-up, at which point, if it’s still alive, it loses interest.

Attacks.Name: Sharp nibbling beaks

Attacks.Name: Arctic bite

Abilities.Name: Shatterer
Abilities.Description: Death can cause fluid-filled sacks inside the barbellite to explode. When the attack roll that kills the barbellite is a natural even roll, each nearby creature takes 10 cold damage.

Attacks.Name: Würm glaciation
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: The target and one other nearby enemy takes 18 cold damage as the area freezes over. Miss: The target and one other nearby enemy takes 6 cold damage.

Attacks.Name: Trilling vibrations (1d3 nearby enemies in a group)
Attacks.Triggers: Limited use: The remorhaz can use trilling vibrations only when the escalation die is odd.

Abilities.Name: Burrow

Abilities.Name: Massive heat absorption

Abilities.Name: Shatterer
Abilities.Description: Death can cause fluid-filled sacks inside the frost-würm to explode. When the attack roll that kills the frost-würm is a natural even roll, each nearby creature takes 20 cold damage.

Abilities.Name: Furnace aura

Abilities.Description:
The remorhaz has glowing “jewels” on its armored plates. When a nearby or far away enemy misses with an attack against the remorhaz, that enemy chooses one: It takes 10 fire damage; OR one piece of its non-magical equipment (something useful, but player’s choice) melts or burns up. Adjust skill checks or stats accordingly. Remorhaz steamer: The remorhaz is melting the ice/snow all the time and obscuring steam rises into the air. Ranged attacks

against the remorhaz take a –2 penalty, or a –4 penalty if the attacker is far away. Spiney remorhaz: The remorhaz is covered in red-hot spines. When a nearby enemy rolls a natural 1–5 with an attack roll, it takes 20 fire damage unless it has somehow protected itself from the heat.

Attacks.Name: Bite and trample

Attacks.Triggers: Miss: The target and each other creature engaged with the remorhaz takes 20 fire damage.

Attacks.Name: Ranged: Nova blast (1d3 nearby enemies)
Attacks.Triggers: Miss: 25 fire damage.

Abilities.Name: Furnace aura

Abilities.Name: Sluggish initiative
Abilities.Description: The queen may be sluggish after eating unsuccessful suitors, laying eggs, or moving across the ice like a rushing avalanche. Roll 2d10 to determine her current initiative.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Bejeweled remorhaz

Remorhaz steamer: The remorhaz is melting the ice/snow all the time and obscuring steam rises into the air. When a nearby enemy rolls a natural 1–5 with an attack roll, it takes 30 fire damage unless it has somehow protected itself from the heat.

Attacks.Name: Caustic bite (one creature wearing light armor or no armor)
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 16+: The target is now considered to be wearing no armor (the armor is damaged beyond repair; adjust defenses accordingly). If the target’s armor is magical, the target must roll a hard save (16+). On a success, the armor isn’t affected. This effect is permanent until the creature obtains new armor.

Attacks.Name: Rusting antenna (one creature wearing heavy armor)
Attacks.Hit: 1 damage, and the target is now considered to be wearing no armor (the armor is damaged beyond repair; adjust defenses accordingly). If the target’s armor is magical, the target must roll a hard save (16+). On a success, the armor isn’t affected. This effect is permanent until the creature obtains new armor.

Abilities.Name: Corrupting body
Abilities.Description: Whenever a creature hits the rust monster with a melee weapon, the attacker must roll a save; on a failure, the weapon is destroyed. Magic weapons require an easy save (6+) instead. This effect is permanent.

Abilities.Name: Rust’s targets
Abilities.Description: Magic items wielded by creatures with 60 hp or more are not affected by the rust monster’s ability to destroy items (but the target still takes damage).

Abilities.Name: Saving quirks
Abilities.Description: Before rolling a save for a magic item, a PC can gain a +5 bonus to the save by agreeing to roleplay the item’s quirk as a huge element of their personality until the next full heal-up. Failure to live up to this roleplaying agreement means that the item hasn’t received the support it needs from its owner to survive the rust monster’s destructive effects, and the item is destroyed at the end of the next battle even if its owner successfully saved.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Big antenna
Abilities.Description: When the rust monster scores a critical hit, it can try to destroy another random magic item in the target’s possession (or a random normal item if the target has no other magic items). The creature must roll a save for the item, as usual.

Attacks.Name: Caustic bite (one creature wearing light armor or no armor)

Abilities.Name: Note
Abilities.Description: Each time the rust monster obliterator destroys heavy armor with this attack, it gains a different random demon ability until the end of the battle (reroll duplicate abilities). (See the demon abilities table.)

Abilities.Name: Corrupting body

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Tail whirligig
Abilities.Description: When an enemy targets the rust monster obliterator with a spell, the rust monster rolls a save. On a success, the spell has no effect on the rust monster. If the rust monster is staggered, it must roll a hard save (16+) instead.

Attacks.Name: Coral-tipped spear
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit against a stuck or hampered enemy: The target takes 1d6 extra damage.

Attacks.Name: Ranged: Hooked net
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: The target is hampered (save ends). Natural odd hit: The target is stuck (save ends). Limited use: 1/battle.

Attacks.Name: Razortoothed jaws

Abilities.Name: Frenzy (group)
Abilities.Description: When two or more razor sharks in the same mob are dropped to 0 hp by an attack, as a free action each dropped razor shark attacks one random nearby non-razor shark creature before it dies. That creature takes 1d8 damage.

Abilities.Name: Water breather
Abilities.Description: Sharks breathe underwater and swim very well. They’re not so good out of sea water (even if they jump), so treat them as semi-hazardous terrain while they’re busy thrashing to death outside the water.

Attacks.Name: Trident and bite (2 attacks)
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 20: Increase the escalation die by 1, and the target is hampered (makes only basic attacks) until the end of its next turn.

Attacks.Name: Ranged: Barbed crossbow (one nearby enemy, or a far away enemy at –2 atk)

Abilities.Name: Blood frenzy
Abilities.Description: Make a note of the escalation die when the sahuagin becomes staggered. The sahuagin gains a bonus to its melee attacks and damage equal to the escalation die value for the rest of the battle.

Abilities.Name: Water breather

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Demon-touched
Abilities.Description: Roll a d6 on the demon abilities table. The sahuagin gains that ability.

Attacks.Name: Coral rod
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit or miss: The priest teleports the target next to one of its nearby allies that it can see, who engages it as a free action. It can’t teleport the target to a location that causes it direct damage (so into a pool of flaming oil is out, but off a ship into the sea is fine).

Attacks.Name: Ranged: Glowpriest’s prayer (1d3 nearby enemies)
Attacks.Hit: 12 psychic damage, and if the attack hits 2 or more targets, roll 1d8 after the attack for the prayer’s effect 1–2 (Hymn of hate): One random nearby conscious enemy takes 4d6 negative energy damage.

Abilities.Name: 3–4 (Curse of despair)
Abilities.Description: Each target that was hit takes a –2 penalty (non-cumulative) to all saves until the end of the battle. 5–6 (Scream of victory): Until the start of the glowpriest’s next turn, each sahuagin and demon in the battle adds the escalation die to its attacks and the PCs don’t. 7–8 (Word of refuge): Remove the glowpriest from play. At the start of its next turn, return it to play nearby its original location. It gains a +4 bonus to all defenses until the end of its next turn after it returns to play.

Abilities.Name: Water breather

Attacks.Triggers: Natural 16+: The target takes 10 ongoing damage.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Punisher
Abilities.Description: When an enemy intercepts the sahuagin mutant, it takes 4d8 damage from the mutant’s claws and teeth. Ripper: When an enemy makes a melee attack against the sahuagin mutant and rolls a natural odd miss, that enemy takes 2d8 damage.

Attacks.Name: Bite
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: The hound leaves teeth in the wound; the target takes 5 ongoing damage, and the hound takes 1d6 damage.

Abilities.Name: Vulnerability
Abilities.Description: holy

Abilities.Name: Chomp chomp chomp
Abilities.Description: Enemies with a lower initiative than the hound take a –5 penalty to disengage checks against it.

Abilities.Name: Skilled intercept 11+
Abilities.Description: Once per round, an engaged skeletal hound can attempt to pop free and intercept an enemy moving past it. Roll a normal save; on 11+, it succeeds.

Attacks.Name: Shortsword
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 16+: The target moves down 1d3 points in initiative order, to a minimum of 1. Natural even miss: 5 damage.

Abilities.Name: Press advantage
Abilities.Description: The legionnaire deals +1d8 damage with its attacks against enemies that have a lower initiative than it.

Attacks.Name: Claws
Attacks.Hit: 2 damage, and the stirge can make a draining probe attack against the target during its next turn if it’s still engaged with the target

Attacks.Name: [Special trigger] Draining probe (one enemy hit by claws last turn)

Abilities.Name: Flight
Abilities.Description: Stirges fly well. Also, the pitch of their wings is high and thin, allowing a stirge to get very close without tipping off its prey.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: One and done
Abilities.Description: After hitting a living creature that has blood with its draining probe attack, the stirge heals 5 hit points and will use its next turn to move, fleeing to the hive to feed the stirgelings…and to alert the hive that there is an easy meal nearby. A new full-strength stirge enters the battle during the next round on the same initiative count.

Attacks.Name: Ranged: Barbed stinger (one nearby enemy)
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 16+: One stirge ally engaged with the target can make a melee attack against it as a free action.

Abilities.Name: Flight
Abilities.Description: The archer stirge flies faster and higher than a normal stirge, but on louder wings.

Attacks.Name: Close: Gooey bloody spray (1d4 nearby enemies)
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit or miss: The target is stuck (save ends). Natural odd hit or miss: The cobbler stirge takes 3 damage.

Abilities.Name: Painful flight
Abilities.Description: The cobbler has stubby ill-proportioned wings and takes 1d6 damage at the end of each round that it flies during battle.

Attacks.Name: Claws
Attacks.Hit: The effect depends on the roll
Attacks.Triggers: Natural odd hit: 2 damage. Natural even hit: Choose one effect, and then the stirgeling mob takes 4 damage (killing this creature first).

Abilities.Name: Regular stirgeling
Abilities.Description: The target takes 3 damage, and 3 ongoing damage. Archer stirgeling: The target takes 6 damage. Cobbler stirgeling: The target takes 3 damage and is stuck until end of its next turn.

Abilities.Name: Flight
Abilities.Description: They aren’t strong fliers but they are quick and agile.

Attacks.Name: Soul flensing tentacles
Attacks.Hit: 30 damage Natural even hit, or any hit against a weakened, stunned, or confused target: Randomly select one of the target’s limited-use powers or spells. The soul flenser flenses it away, removing it from the target until that creature regains it via a successful connection to the oversoul (see below).
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 3, 6, or 9: The target is confused (save ends).

Attacks.Name: Close: Soul blast (1d4 nearby enemies in a group)
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: The target is weakened (save ends). Natural odd hit: If the target is already weakened, it’s also stunned until end of its next turn. Natural 3, 6, or 9: The target is confused (save ends).

Abilities.Name: Connection to the Oversoul
Abilities.Description: When a creature slays a soul flenser, it can roll a hard save (16+). If it succeeds, the creature regains one power it has had flensed away.

Abilities.Name: Intellect fortress
Abilities.Description: When an enemy misses the soul flenser with an attack against MD, that attacker takes half the miss damage, if any.

Abilities.Name: Underkraken teleport
Abilities.Description: A soul flenser that has successfully flensed at least once can (and usually will, provided some of its enemies are confused, weakened, or stunned) use a standard action to prepare itself to teleport. Once it does this, during its next turn it can use a move action to teleport back to its home underkraken, no matter how distant, leaving the battle behind. Soul flensers fighting beside or within their underkraken can’t use this ability; they’re already home.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Flensing escalator
Abilities.Description: The soul flenser gains an attack bonus equal to the escalation die against creatures that have had one or more powers flensed away. Oversoul control: While confused by a soul flenser’s effect, a creature that has had a power flensed away can use and re-use that limited power against their erstwhile allies, if the GM sees how to use the power in a useful way.

Attacks.Name: Fists, claws, or shoddy weapons
Attacks.Hit: 20 damage, or 40 damage against a target that currently has one more powers flensed away.

Abilities.Name: Connection to the Oversoul
Abilities.Description: When a creature slays one of the flensed, it can roll a hard save (16+). If it succeeds, the creature regains one power it had flensed away.

Abilities.Name: Flensing escalator
Abilities.Description: The Flensed gains an attack bonus equal to the escalation die against creatures that have had one or more powers flensed away.

Attacks.Name: All-enveloping toothy maw
Attacks.Triggers: Natural even hit: The tarrasque grabs the target. It will swallow a grabbed enemy in 1d3 rounds (see swallow whole). Natural 16+: The tarrasque swallows the target immediately (see swallow whole).

Attacks.Name: Immense spike, horn, or tusk
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 16+: The target takes 9d6 extra damage and pops free from the tarrasque as it’s hurled far away.

Attacks.Name: Close: Earth-shaking, taloned claw (each nearby enemy in a group)
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 16+: The target is stunned (save ends). Miss: The target is dazed (save ends).

Attacks.Name: Close: Cataclysmic tail slam (each nearby enemy in a group)
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 16+: The target is vulnerable (save ends). Miss: The target is dazed until the end of its next turn.

Attacks.Name: Drag (each creature on its back)
Attacks.Hit: 130 damage, the target pops free of the tarrasque, and the target is hampered (save ends)

Attacks.Name: Collapse (each creature in/on the structure)
Attacks.Hit: 90 damage, and the target is stuck and takes 20 ongoing damage (hard save ends both, 16+)

Attacks.Name: Gullet digestion
Attacks.Hit: 80 acid damage, and 20 ongoing acid damage
Attacks.Triggers: Miss: 5d12 acid damage.

Abilities.Name: Amphibious
Abilities.Description: The tarrasque can swim and breathe underwater (or it holds so much air in its vast lungs that it makes no difference).

Abilities.Name: Enormously bulky
Abilities.Description: The tarrasque is so huge that it ignores opportunity attacks. In addition, normal-sized enemies are like fleas to it, and disengaging from the tarrasque requires only an easy save (6+), unless the target is grabbed.

Abilities.Name: Immortal
Abilities.Description: The tarrasque can’t be killed, save by the explicit will of a god (and not some jumped-up local god, either) or, perhaps, the sacrifice of a great icon. The tarrasque’s HP total indicates the amount of damage required to make it disgorge swallowed enemies and flee to go hibernate while it regenerates the damage it suffered and decide if it wants to rampage again.

Abilities.Name: Inflexible
Abilities.Description: The tarrasque can’t easily fight foes that get onto its back, and may not even notice them if they aren’t attacking it. When it does tire of a passenger, it can either use its tail slam attack (–2 attack penalty: on a hit, the target only takes half damage and is knocked off the tarrasque [possibly falling damage]; on a miss, the target takes no damage) or a drag attack as a standard action, crushing the rider between its shell and a mountainside or other high, hard obstacle.

Abilities.Name: Legendary resistance
Abilities.Description:
The tarrasque is immune to normal conditions and effects (stunned, weakened, etc.), but it isn’t completely impervious. Bypassing its resistances requires icon-supported effort. A PC can use one 5 or 6 they acquired from icon relationship dice rolls to overcome the resistance each time they use an attack or power that would apply a condition or

effect upon the tarrasque. Of course, they must also provide a story to go along with the reason the tarrasque is affected.

Abilities.Name: Leveler
Abilities.Description: When the escalation die is even, as a move action the tarrasque can demolish any ordinary structure it can reach, such as a house, castle wall, temple, or ship. The beast automatically reduces the structure to rubble, rendering it useless. Each creature on top of or within the structure is subject to a collapse attack.

Abilities.Name: Swallow whole
Abilities.Description: Once a creature is swallowed, it goes inside one of the tarrasque’s gigantic stomachs. It can still act while inside the tarrasque, but it will have to deal with the beast’s stomach acid that is splashing around. A swallowed creature must deal 400 damage to the tarrasque to force it to disgorge the contents of its gullet, freeing the creature. During the tarrasque’s turn, it can make a gullet digestion attack against the target as a free action.

Abilities.Name: Soft-ish innerbelly
Abilities.Description: The tarrasque doesn’t have scales on the inside. It takes a –5 penalty to all defenses against attacks from inside its gullet, though only melee and close attacks can be made in there. The tarrasque’s insides are immune to acid damage, however.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Fear
Abilities.Description:
While engaged with the tarrasque, enemies that have 216 hp or fewer are dazed (–4 attack) and do not add the escalation die to their attacks. Regeneration 230: While a tarrasque is damaged, its malign magical flesh heals 230 hit points at the start of the tarrasque’s turn. It can regenerate five times per battle. If it heals up to its maximum hit points, then that use of regeneration doesn’t

count against the five-use limit. With this power, the monstrosity is likely unstoppable without a powerful magical artifact designed specifically to bind, wound, or otherwise hamper the tarrasque.

Attacks.Name: Gauntlet slap
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 5, 10, 15, 20: The target also takes 3 ongoing psychic damage.

Attacks.Name: Ranged: Orb of pain (one or more nearby or far away enemies; see history of abuse)
Attacks.Triggers: Natural 5, 10, 15, 20: The target also takes 3 ongoing psychic damage.

Abilities.Name: Beyond saving
Abilities.Description: The avenging orb takes a –5 penalty to saving throws.

Abilities.Name: History of abuse
Abilities.Description: Keep track of the number of enemy attacks that hit the avenging orb during the battle. Until the end of the battle, the avenging orb can target an additional enemy beyond the first with its orb of pain attack for each of those hits. (Note that avenging orbs engaged in melee usually choose to use orb of pain and suffer any resulting opportunity attacks; if they’re lucky they’ll survive the attack and be able to choose more targets for the orb of pain.)

Attacks.Name: Cheap greatsword
Attacks.Triggers: Natural odd hit: The target takes extra damage equal to half the amount the destroying sword took from the last attack that hit it this battle.

Attacks.Name: Ranged: Shortbow (one nearby or far away enemy)

Abilities.Name: Beyond saving
Abilities.Description: The destroying sword takes a –5 penalty to saving throws.

Attacks.Name: Steel hammer
Attacks.Triggers: Miss: 1d4 damage.

Abilities.Name: Anguished interceptor
Abilities.Description: When an enduring shield is engaged and an enemy attempts to move past it, the enduring shield can roll a disengage check to intercept it as an interrupt action (once per round). If the attempt fails, the enduring shield takes 1d6 psychic damage.

Abilities.Name: Beyond saving
Abilities.Description: The enduring shield takes a –5 penalty to saving throws.

Abilities.Name: Supernatural endurance
Abilities.Description: When an attack hits the enduring shield, it gains a +5 bonus to the defense that the attack targeted until the end of the battle or until another attack hits it, in which case the bonus switches to the defense most recently hit.

Abilities.Name: Hardwood resistance
Abilities.Description: This creature has resist damage 12+ to all damage except fire damage and melee weapon damage, which damages it normally.

Attacks.Name: Grasping branches

Attacks.Name: [Special trigger] Twist and snap (includes +4 grab bonus) vs. PD

Abilities.Name: Fire fire fire!
Abilities.Description: When the treant takes 15 or more fire damage from a single attack, it releases all grabbed creatures.

Abilities.Name: Hardwood resistance
Abilities.Description: This creature has resist damage 12+ to all damage except fire damage and melee weapon damage, which damages it normally.

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Toxic haze
Abilities.Description: The treant exudes a toxic cloud of pollen. When an enemy engages the treant or starts its turn engaged with the treant, it takes 4 poison damage.

Attacks.Name: Grasping branches (2 attacks)
Attacks.Hit: 30 damage, and the treant grabs the target. When the treant starts its turn grabbing an enemy, it can make a twist and snap attack against that target as a standard action that turn.

Attacks.Name: [Special trigger] Twist and snap (includes +4 grab bonus) vs. PD
Attacks.Hit: 80 damage, and the target is dazed (save ends). If the treant starts its turn grabbing a dazed enemy, it can make a titanic rend attack against that target as a standard action that turn.
Attacks.Triggers: Miss: 40 damage.

Attacks.Name: [Special trigger] Titanic rend (includes +4 grab bonus) vs. PD
Attacks.Hit: 160 damage, and the treant titan can continue making titanic rend attacks against the target until it escapes the grab, at which point the treant will have to use a grasping branches attack against it again.

Abilities.Name: Fire fire fire!
Abilities.Description: When the treant takes 35 or more fire damage from a single attack, it releases all grabbed creatures.

Abilities.Name: Hardwood resistance

Abilities.Name: Nastier: Coffin of living wood
Abilities.Description: When the treant titan hits with a titanic rend attack, the target is pulled into a hollow chamber within the treant. While grabbed by the treant this way, the target can’t be the target of its allies’ powers or spells. Gauntlet of branches: Countless smaller branches whip through the air around the treant titan. When a creature engaged with the treant misses it with an attack, that creature takes 12 damage from the whipping branches.

Abilities.Name: Chameleon
